capability_investigated:
generate(features, prompts, **kwargs) and how WhisperProcessor builds
input_features — specifically whether the prompts list and a list-input to
the processor support batching multiple 30s windows in one decode call.
what_i_learned:
The stub decodes only one 30s window, so all audio past 30s is deleted on
multi-minute 0715 calls. The backend's generate already accepts a list of
prompts (one per batched feature row), and processor(list_of_arrays) returns
batched input_features — so consecutive 30s windows can be decoded as one
batch without leaving the frozen surface.
hypothesis:
Split audio into consecutive 30s windows, batch them through a single
generate call with one prompt per window, and join the decoded texts. This
recovers the deleted tail and should raise length_ratio.p05 and sharply
lower corpus_cer from the deletion-dominated baseline.

capability_investigated:
The processor() feature-extraction step and the generate() decode call, used
per-window in a sequential loop rather than batched — i.e. whether manual
pre-slicing of the waveform reaches audio that the single-window stub deletes.
what_i_learned:
The frozen WhisperProcessor pads/truncates any input to exactly one 30s window
(3000 mel frames), so feeding full multi-minute audio silently drops every
sample past 30s; manual pre-slicing into 30s chunks is the only way to reach
later audio through the frozen surface. generate() can be called once per slice
without batching, avoiding whatever made iter_001's batch decode emit no report.
hypothesis:
Loop over consecutive 30s windows, decode each independently, and join the
transcripts. This directly addresses the deletion-dominant failure mode by
recovering the long-form tail, using a sequential mechanism distinct from the
rejected batch-decode attempt.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s **decoding_kwargs pass-through to ctranslate2 Whisper.generate —
specifically the n-gram repetition control (no_repeat_ngram_size) that the
current greedy decode (beam_size=1, sampling_temperature=0.0) never sets.
what_i_learned:
generate() forwards arbitrary decode kwargs untouched, so no_repeat_ngram_size
is reachable through the frozen surface. The diagnosis shows repeated_text on
4/11 files co-occurring with length_ratio well below 1 on every file: a greedy
n-gram loop inside a 30s chunk consumes the per-chunk decode budget repeating a
phrase, which produces BOTH the flagged repetition AND the downstream deletion
(the loop terminates the chunk before the remaining speech is transcribed).
hypothesis:
Set no_repeat_ngram_size=3 on the per-chunk decode to block the 3-gram loops.
Breaking the loop frees decode budget so the rest of each chunk gets
transcribed, which should lift length_ratio (less deletion) and clear the
repeated_text flag at once — a single decode-kwarg mechanism, negligible
runtime cost, no change to the chunking already in the ledger.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s **decoding_kwargs pass-through to ctranslate2 Whisper.generate —
specifically beam_size/patience/length_penalty, none of which engage under the
beam_size=1 greedy path that every prior iteration (001-003) used.
what_i_learned:
The decode is pure greedy in all prior iters; greedy with beam_size=1 is the
config most vulnerable to the repeat-then-early-EOT collapse that explains the
universal length_ratio<1 (0.32-0.81 on every file), not just the 4 repeated_text
files. Beam search is reachable via the frozen surface and keeps competing
hypotheses alive past greedy's premature EOT commitment.
hypothesis:
Switch beam_size 1 -> 5. Beam search reduces both the universal deletion
(recovers tail lost to early EOT) and the secondary repetition, addressing the
dominant length_ratio signal without the diversity-forcing side effects that
made iter_003's no_repeat_ngram worse.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s stochastic-sampling path — beam_size=1 with sampling_topk>1 and
sampling_temperature>0 — which every prior iter (001-004) left unused by
decoding only deterministically (greedy or beam_size=5, temperature=0.0).
what_i_learned:
The frozen generate() forwards sampling_topk/sampling_temperature untouched,
so the same features can be re-decoded stochastically without leaving the
surface. This is the missing counterpart to the iter_003 finding: a
deterministic decode that loops on a phrase is stuck there, but a temperature
sample over the same chunk takes a different path and can escape the loop —
recovering the chunk tail that the repeat had deleted (length_ratio < 1).
hypothesis:
After the beam decode, detect a collapsed chunk via low unique-eojeol ratio
(<0.45 over >=20 tokens) and re-decode just that chunk with stochastic
sampling (beam_size=1, sampling_topk=5, sampling_temperature=0.8), keeping the
sample only if it is no longer collapsed. Targets the 4 repeated_text files
and their co-occurring deletion without the n-gram ban that regressed iter_003.

capability_investigated:
The prompt-token list passed to generate() — specifically the
"<|notimestamps|>" decoder directive that every prior iter (001-005)
hard-coded, vs. Whisper's native timestamped decoding mode reachable by
simply omitting that token from the prompt.
what_i_learned:
The frozen surface lets the workspace fully control the decoder prompt
composition, so "<|notimestamps|>" is optional. With it present (all prior
iters) the decoder has no in-window segment anchor and is free to emit EOT
early — consistent with the universal length_ratio<1 (0.37-0.82 on every
file) that beam search and temperature sampling never moved. Omitting it puts
the model in timestamped long-form mode, and since timestamp tokens are
special tokens, skip_special_tokens=True still returns clean text.
hypothesis:
Drop "<|notimestamps|>" from the prompt so each 30s window is decoded in
timestamped mode. The "<|t|>" segment markers keep the decoder emitting until
the window is covered, fighting the within-chunk early-EOT deletion that
dominates the diagnosis (length_ratio ~0.6 on all 11 files). All decode
kwargs (beam_size=5) are left at the best iter_004 config to isolate the
mechanism.

capability_investigated:
The timestamp token values inside results[0].sequences_ids[0] — the <|t|>
markers iter_006 enabled by dropping <|notimestamps|> but never read,
discarding them via skip_special_tokens=True. Probed how to identify them
(tid >= convert_tokens_to_ids("<|0.00|>"), the highest vocab ids, above EOT)
and convert to audio time (0.02s per token).
what_i_learned:
The decoded sequence carries per-segment end timestamps as ordinary token ids
above the <|0.00|> id; the last such id marks the end of the last complete
segment in the 30s window. This means the fixed +30s stride is not forced —
the window can be re-anchored to that segment boundary, and the trailing
truncated segment (which Whisper systematically declines to emit, the residual
length_ratio<1 cause) can be left for the next, re-anchored window.
hypothesis:
Replace the blind 30s stride with Whisper's native long-form loop: keep only
text up to the last timestamp marker, drop the truncated trailing segment, and
advance seek to that marker's audio time so the next window re-decodes the cut
tail from a clean segment start. Removes boundary deletion without duplicating
audio; the final window keeps full text so the call tail is not dropped.

capability_investigated:
Whisper's <|startofprev|> prompt slot — the previous-text conditioning
mechanism (faster-whisper's condition_on_previous_text). Every prior iter
(001-007) decoded each 30s window in complete isolation, passing only
[<|sot|>, <|ko|>, <|transcribe|>] and discarding cross-window context. The
frozen surface lets the workspace compose any prompt list (iter_006), so a
prev-text prefix is reachable without extra decode passes.
what_i_learned:
The decoder prompt can carry a <|startofprev|> token followed by prior text
tokens ([startofprev, *prev_tokens, sot, lang, task]); ctranslate2
Whisper.generate forwards this prompt verbatim, so running transcript context
is injectable through the frozen surface at zero added compute (the prev
tokens ride the same generate call rather than adding passes). This is the
conditioning counterpart to iter_007's timestamp anchoring — the latter fixed
deletion (length_ratio now 0.91-0.98), leaving the substitution residual that
context conditioning targets.
hypothesis:
Prepend the previously decoded transcript (capped at 224 tokens, reset on an
empty window) as <|startofprev|> context to each window's prompt. With
deletion solved, the dominant remaining error is substitution; cross-window
context disambiguates recurring call-center/insurance vocabulary and
stabilizes spelling at window boundaries, lowering CER without changing
runtime or window advancement.

capability_investigated:
ctranslate2 Whisper.generate's length_penalty kwarg — the beam
length-normalization exponent. Every prior iter (004 onward) used beam_size=5
but left length_penalty at its default of 1.0, so the normalization itself was
never exercised even though beam search was active.
what_i_learned:
The frozen generate() forwards length_penalty untouched, and it only engages
under beam search (beam_size>1), which the current best already uses. ct2 scores
beams as sum_logprob / length**length_penalty, so at the default exponent of 1
the cumulative negative log-prob still net-penalizes longer hypotheses — the
surface mechanism behind the residual universal length_ratio<1 (0.91-0.98 on
every file) that iter_007's re-anchoring left behind. This knob is independent
of beam_size (iter_004) and of the prompt composition (iter_006/008).
hypothesis:
Set length_penalty=1.2 on the beam decode. The diagnosis residual is a mild,
systematic in-window deletion present on all 11 files; shifting the
length-normalized score above the default exponent makes the beam prefer the
longer hypothesis, recovering the tokens it was dropping per window without
changing the long-form re-anchoring loop or adding decode passes (runtime
neutral).

capability_investigated:
The ctranslate2 WhisperGenerationResult's no_speech_prob field, requested via
generate()'s documented return_no_speech_prob kwarg. Every prior iter (001-009)
read only sequences_ids and tuned decode params; none requested or consumed the
encoder's per-window no-speech estimate.
what_i_learned:
generate() forwards return_no_speech_prob=True untouched, and results[0] then
exposes a float no_speech_prob per decoded window — the encoder's probability
that the 30s span contains no speech. This is reachable through the frozen
surface and is the standard Whisper signal for the hallucination_hit failure
mode (text confabulated over silence), which is now the residual the
timestamp-anchored loop left behind.
hypothesis:
Gate each window's transcript on no_speech_prob: when it exceeds Whisper's
standard 0.6 threshold the window is non-speech, so I drop its (hallucinated)
text and advance a full chunk instead of joining it. This targets the two
diagnosis focus files (both flagged hallucination_hit) without altering the
long-form path on genuine speech windows.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s return_scores kwarg and the resulting results[0].scores field —
the decoder's length-normalized sequence avg-logprob. Distinct from iter_010's
encoder no_speech_prob; every prior iter ran a single deterministic beam pass
per window and threw this confidence signal away.
what_i_learned:
generate() forwards return_scores=True untouched and results[0].scores[0] then
carries a float per hypothesis: the cumulative log-prob normalized by
length**length_penalty (~avg logprob, negative). This is the standard
openai-whisper decode-quality signal — a low value marks the windows where the
beam committed to a low-confidence (substitution-heavy / partial-hallucination)
transcript, which the timestamp loop alone left as the residual on the cer
0.21-0.29 files (length_ratio 0.91-0.93 vs 0.95-0.98 on clean files).
hypothesis:
Add Whisper's canonical temperature-fallback on top of iter_007's anchoring:
beam pass at temp 0 with return_scores; if its score is below -1.0, re-decode
the same features at rising temperature (0.4, 0.8) via sampling and keep the
best-scoring attempt. Sampling escapes the beam's bad local optimum on exactly
the low-confidence windows that drive substitution, while clean windows still
cost one beam pass so the runtime budget holds.

capability_investigated:
Requesting both return_no_speech_prob=True and return_scores=True in the same
generate() call, and reading results[0].no_speech_prob (encoder non-speech
prob, iter_010) together with results[0].scores[0] (decoder length-normalized
avg log-prob, iter_011) from one decode — the two confidence signals neither
prior iter combined.
what_i_learned:
Both fields are populated on the same WhisperGenerationResult from a single
generate() pass (no extra decode, no runtime cost), so the joint openai-whisper
silence rule (no_speech_prob > 0.6 AND avg_logprob < -1.0) is computable per
window through the frozen surface. The AND is the discovery: either field alone
(iter_010/iter_011) misfires on real-speech windows and over-deletes, which is
why both tied/regressed; requiring both to fire restricts the drop to the
confabulated-over-silence windows that the hallucination_hit focus files hit.
hypothesis:
On the timestamp-anchored iter_007 loop, skip a (non-final) window's text only
when no_speech_prob > 0.6 AND avg_logprob < -1.0, advancing a full chunk. This
removes the hallucinated spans on the two hallucination_hit focus files while
the conservative AND protects legitimate-speech windows from the length_ratio
loss that single-signal gating caused.

capability_investigated:
The full results[0].sequences_ids LIST and results[0].scores LIST returned by
generate() under beam search. Every prior iter (001-012) read only
sequences_ids[0] (the single top beam) and discarded beams 1..N. Probed that
num_hypotheses controls how many beams are returned and that return_scores
populates one length-normalized avg-logprob per returned beam, sorted best-first.
what_i_learned:
generate() with num_hypotheses=beam_size returns all N beams as a list (no extra
decode pass — beam search already computed them), and return_scores gives a
parallel score list sorted descending. Because ct2 scores beams as
sum_logprob / length**length_penalty (iter_009), the top beam is systematically
the SHORTER of near-equal hypotheses — so the always-discarded longer beams are a
reachable, zero-cost lever against the universal length_ratio<1 deletion residual.
hypothesis:
Select, among the returned beams, the longest one whose score is within 0.10
avg-logprob of the best, instead of always taking sequences_ids[0]. This recovers
the tail clipped by length normalization (the dominant residual on the cer
0.21-0.29 files, all length_ratio 0.91-0.93) while the confidence margin blocks
low-probability/hallucinated beams. Grafts cleanly onto iter_007's timestamp loop.

capability_investigated:
The <|startofprev|> prompt slot (ledger iter_008) used with a FIXED static
payload rather than the running decoded transcript. Studied how the frozen
surface lets the workspace compose an arbitrary prompt id list passed verbatim
to ct2 Whisper.generate, and how the prev-text segment re-weights decoder
token priors independently of the per-window audio.
what_i_learned:
The prev-text payload in the <|startofprev|> slot does not have to be the
prior window's output. A constant string tokenized with
tokenizer.encode(add_special_tokens=False) and prepended as
[startofprev, *glossary, sot, lang, task] is forwarded verbatim and is
identical for every window, so it carries the prior-conditioning *bias*
(the lever iter_008 reached for) WITHOUT the window-to-window error cascade
that made iter_008's running-transcript feed regress and get rejected.
hypothesis:
The dominant residual is in-domain term substitution on the hard files
(cer 0.21-0.29, length_ratio ~0.92 — deletion already fixed by iter_007).
Prepending a fixed Korean insurance call-center glossary into <|startofprev|>
biases the decoder toward correct domain spellings (보험료/약관/특약/피보험자
...) at zero added compute, attacking substitution where every decode-param
knob (beam/temp/length_penalty/no_speech/scores/num_hypotheses) has stalled.

capability_investigated:
The interaction between timestamp-anchored re-anchoring (iter_007) and where
each window physically starts in the waveform. Studied that the frozen
surface lets the workspace choose the window's start sample freely and that
results[0].sequences_ids[0] carries per-segment end timestamps (ledger
iter_007) that give each segment an ABSOLUTE audio time once offset by the
window's start — enough to dedup overlapping content by time rather than text.
what_i_learned:
Re-anchoring to the last complete segment makes the next window begin exactly
at a hard segment cut, so its first new segment is decoded with zero preceding
audio; Whisper clips the onset of an utterance it hears cold, which is a
within-window deletion the boundary fix cannot reach (length_ratio stuck at
0.91-0.98 on every file, no longer a gap problem). Because each segment's end
timestamp plus the window's start sample yields an absolute time, an
overlap-back window can be deduped by timestamp (end_abs <= consumed_time ->
drop) with no text matching and no extra decode pass — the stride stays the
per-segment advance, so window count and runtime are unchanged.
hypothesis:
Start each window _OVERLAP_SECONDS before the consumed point so the first new
segment gets real acoustic left-context (recovering the clipped onsets behind
the residual length_ratio<1), and discard the re-heard already-committed
segments by their absolute timestamp end-time. Stride remains the segment
advance, keeping runtime flat while recovering the within-window deletion that
re-anchoring alone left on the worst files (cer 0.21-0.29, length_ratio ~0.92).

capability_investigated:
ctranslate2 Whisper.generate's max_initial_timestamp_index kwarg (default 50,
= 1.0s at 0.02s/token), forwarded untouched through frozen generate()'s
**decoding_kwargs. Every prior iter (001-015) left it at the default, so the
decoder was always free to emit its first segment timestamp anywhere in the
first second of each window.
what_i_learned:
max_initial_timestamp_index caps how late the FIRST timestamp token may fall,
i.e. how much leading audio the decoder is permitted to skip before
transcribing. At the default 50 the model may discard up to 1.0s of onset.
Because iter_007 re-anchoring starts every non-first window exactly at a hard
segment cut (utterance onset, no preceding audio — iter_015's cold-onset
finding), that 1s grace is precisely where the residual leading deletion
hides. The knob is reachable through the frozen surface and is independent of
beam_size, length_penalty, and prompt composition.
hypothesis:
Set max_initial_timestamp_index=0 so the first segment of every window is
pinned to <|0.00|>, forbidding the leading-onset skip. This forces the model
to transcribe the cold onset at each re-anchored boundary, targeting the
universal length_ratio<1 (0.91-0.98) that beam/length-penalty/timestamp
re-anchoring all left behind, without overlap, dedup, or extra decode passes
(the regression cause of iter_015's overlap-back approach).

capability_investigated:
generate()'s repetition_penalty kwarg, named explicitly in the frozen
asr_backend docstring's **decoding_kwargs list but never set by any prior
iter. Distinct from iter_003's no_repeat_ngram_size: that is a HARD ban on
repeating any n-gram, whereas repetition_penalty is a SOFT multiplicative
divisor applied to the logits of already-emitted tokens during beam search.
what_i_learned:
ct2 Whisper.generate forwards repetition_penalty untouched through the frozen
surface and it engages on the active beam_size=5 path. It down-weights tokens
already present in a beam's prefix at every step, so a beam tempted into the
repeat-then-premature-EOT collapse (iter_003's diagnosed deletion mechanism,
the cause of the uniform length_ratio<1 that survives the timestamp loop) is
nudged off the loop continuously rather than only blocked at an exact n-gram
match. It is independent of beam_size, length_penalty, and prompt composition.
hypothesis:
Add repetition_penalty=1.1 to the single per-window beam decode. The residual
is now a UNIFORM mild under-generation (length_ratio 0.91-0.98 on every file,
worst 0.91-0.93 on the high-CER 01_8088/01_8098 calls). A soft per-token reuse
penalty discourages the within-window repeat that consumes the decode budget
and triggers early EOT, recovering deleted tail across all files and easing the
flagged repeated_text file (8016) — at zero added decode passes, runtime-neutral.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s return_scores=True scores list (iter_011) used as a RE-DECODE
TRIGGER rather than just read, combined with conditional temperature
escalation (beam_size=1, sampling_topk=0, sampling_temperature>0 — iter_005's
sampling path) within one window. This is the assembled faster-whisper
generate_with_fallback control loop, never built by any prior iter.
what_i_learned:
results[0].scores[0] (length-normalized avg-logprob) and the text's zlib
compression_ratio together form a per-window quality gate computable entirely
through the frozen surface from a single beam pass. Prior iters either read
scores passively (iter_011) or sampled unconditionally (iter_005); neither
gated a re-decode on the signal, so the low-confidence windows the temp-0 beam
committed to (the substitution residual on the cer 0.21-0.29 files) were never
given a second, diversified decode. The fallback fires only on gate-failing
windows, so extra passes are confined to bad audio.
hypothesis:
On windows where scores[0] < -1.0 or compression_ratio > 2.4, escalate
temperature (0.0 -> 0.4 -> 0.8) and keep the highest-scoring hypothesis. The
temp-0 beam's degenerate/low-confidence commitment on the worst files is
exactly what avg_logprob flags; a tempered sample takes a different path and
can recover a higher-confidence transcript, lowering substitution CER without
touching the clean windows or the winning timestamp-anchor loop.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s num_hypotheses kwarg on the SAMPLING path (beam_size=1,
sampling_temperature>0), as opposed to iter_013's use of it on the beam
path. Studied that ct2 returns num_hypotheses independent samples per
generate call with one return_scores avg-logprob each.
what_i_learned:
With beam_size=1 and sampling_temperature>0, num_hypotheses=N makes ct2 draw
N independent stochastic samples in a single decode call, each with its own
length-normalized avg-logprob via return_scores. This is exactly
openai-whisper's best_of: the sampled hypotheses are NOT guaranteed sorted,
so the best draw must be selected by max(score) explicitly. iter_018's
fallback drew only one sample per temperature and kept it blindly.
hypothesis:
The two worst files (cer 0.28 / 0.255, length_ratio 0.92-0.93, no
hallucination/repeat flags) are the low-confidence windows that trip the
iter_018 gate, where a single temperature draw can commit to a poor
transcript. Drawing _BEST_OF=5 samples and keeping the highest-avg-logprob
one (real best_of) gives those windows multiple shots and selects the
strongest, lowering substitution on the hard files. Extra cost stays
confined to gate-failing windows.

capability_investigated:
ct2 Whisper.generate's `patience` kwarg (beam-search patience factor, Kasai
et al. 2022), forwarded untouched through frozen generate()'s
**decoding_kwargs. Every prior iter (001-019) left it at the default 1.0, so
beam search always finalized as soon as `beam_size` complete hypotheses were
found — the search never explored past that first batch of EOT commitments.
what_i_learned:
patience is distinct from length_penalty (iter_009): length_penalty re-scores
already-found beams by length, whereas patience changes HOW MANY complete
hypotheses the search collects before stopping (beam_size * patience). At the
default 1.0 the search halts at the first 5 finished beams, which on the
greedy-prone early-EOT path are systematically the shortest ones; raising it
forces the search to keep expanding and surface the longer candidates that
finish later. It only engages under beam_size>1 (the active temp-0 path) and
is orthogonal to length_penalty and repetition_penalty.
hypothesis:
Set patience=2.0 on the temp-0 beam pass so beam search collects 10 complete
hypotheses before finalizing. The early-finishing short beams that cause the
uniform length_ratio<1 (0.92-0.98 on every file) no longer terminate the
search prematurely, so longer/more-complete transcripts stay competitive for
the return_scores selection — recovering trailing content without changing
prompt composition or stride.

capability_investigated:
The <|startofprev|> prompt slot (ledger iter_008/iter_014) used with the
RUNNING decoded transcript again, but combined with the iter_018 confidence
gate as a reset trigger. Studied that the gate already classifies each
window as confident/degenerate from a single beam pass, and that the frozen
surface forwards an arbitrary [sot_prev, *prev, sot, lang, task] prompt
verbatim with no extra decode pass.
what_i_learned:
iter_008's running-text conditioning and iter_018's quality gate are
composable: the gate's gate_failed signal (avg-logprob < -1.0 or
compression_ratio > 2.4) is exactly the discriminator for whether a window's
text is trustworthy enough to feed forward. So previous-text conditioning can
be made cascade-safe through the frozen surface alone — a low-confidence
window's text is excluded AND clears the prev buffer — which neither iter_008
(no gate, cascaded) nor iter_018 (gate but isolated windows) did.
hypothesis:
Substitution now dominates (length_ratio 0.92-0.96, no flags on the cer
0.21-0.28 files); context conditioning targets substitution. Prepend the
running transcript (capped to last 200 tokens) via <|startofprev|>, and clear
it whenever a window trips the confidence gate, so domain/call context biases
priors without the iter_008 error cascade. Rides the same generate() call, so
runtime is unchanged.

capability_investigated:
The ct2 Whisper object returned by load() — specifically its
detect_language(features) method, a method on the returned object that no
prior iter (001-021) ever called. Every iteration reached the model only
through generate() and hard-coded the <|ko|> language token in the prompt.
what_i_learned:
load() hands back the raw ctranslate2.models.Whisper instance, which exposes
detect_language(features) returning per-row [(lang_token, prob)] sorted
descending from a single decode step (much cheaper than a beam pass). The
language slot in the decoder prompt is therefore not forced to <|ko|> — it
can be conditioned per window on the encoder's own language estimate, a
surface entirely outside the generate() **decoding_kwargs the ledger exhausted.
hypothesis:
The residual is substitution, not deletion (length_ratio is 0.92-0.98 on
every file, yet hard files sit at CER 0.25-0.28). Korean insurance
call-center audio is code-switched (English product names, "OK/no", spoken
digits); a span forced into <|ko|> is transcribed phonetically into wrong
Korean characters. Replacing the hard-coded language token with the
per-window detect_language() result lets English/numeric windows decode in
their detected language, removing that substitution source.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s full beam list under num_hypotheses=beam_size + return_scores
(ledger iter_013): the N>1 beams ct2 already computes but every kept config
discarded by reading only sequences_ids[0]. Studied that ct2 sorts beams
best-score-first and scores them sum_logprob / length**length_penalty.
what_i_learned:
Because the score is length-normalized, the top beam is systematically the
shorter of near-equal hypotheses, so the always-discarded longer beams are a
reachable zero-cost length lever. Crucially the selection can be decoupled
from the fallback gate: gate on scores[0] (trigger rate unchanged) while
keeping a longer beam from the same pass, so runtime is identical to iter_018.
hypothesis:
Keep the longest beam within a 0.15 score-margin of the top (rejecting
compression-ratio>2.4 degenerates) instead of beam 0. iter_013 found this
lever but it was never the kept mechanism; it directly lifts the universal
length_ratio<1 deletion residual that beam/patience/length_penalty did not move.

capability_investigated:
Segment end-timestamp values (ledger iter_007/iter_015) used as ABSOLUTE
audio times (window_start + seg_end) to dedup overlapping windows, rather
than the exact-boundary +advance re-anchor every kept config has used. The
frozen surface returns these markers in sequences_ids[0]; the workspace is
free to choose any window start sample, so a left-overlap re-decode is
reachable with no new generate() kwarg.
what_i_learned:
Re-anchoring to the last complete segment makes the next window begin exactly
at a hard segment cut (cold utterance onset, iter_015), and that onset
clipping is a within-window substitution the boundary fix cannot touch — the
cause of the residual cer 0.21-0.28 on otherwise length-healthy files. The
per-segment end timestamp plus the window start sample yields an absolute
audio time, which lets an overlapping re-decode be deduped by time
(seg_end_abs <= committed_time -> drop) with no text matching and no extra
decode pass beyond the re-heard overlap span.
hypothesis:
Back the next window up by 3s of left context so the boundary segment (and
the previously truncated trailing segment) is decoded with preceding audio
instead of cold, and drop the re-decoded overlap by absolute segment
end-time. This eliminates the cold-onset substitution iter_015 identified
while keeping deletion fixed, at ~10% more windows (within budget).

capability_investigated:
generate()'s suppress_tokens kwarg. ct2 Whisper.generate defaults it to
[-1], which expands to Whisper's built-in non-speech suppression list and is
applied at every decode step. The frozen docstring opens **decoding_kwargs
("...repetition_penalty, sampling_*, ...") so it is reachable, and no prior
iter (001-024) ever set it — it is the one decode-path lever the ledger
never names.
what_i_learned:
suppress_tokens=[-1] is not a no-op: it bans a fixed symbol/non-speech token
set at every step of every window, which is the only decode constraint
applied identically across all windows. That uniformity matches the residual
signature — length_ratio < 1 on EVERY file (0.92-0.98), worst on the
high-CER files (01_8088_10:01=0.924, 01_8098=0.927) — which beam length
tuning (iter_009/013/023), patience (iter_020), and re-anchoring never
closed. Removing the suppression (suppress_tokens=[]) restores those
continuation candidates that were biasing the beam toward earlier EOT.
hypothesis:
Set suppress_tokens=[] on both the temp-0 beam pass and the temperature
fallback samples in _decode_with_fallback, disabling default non-speech
suppression. This is a token-availability length lever orthogonal to
length_penalty, patience, and beam selection: keeping the banned tokens
available lets the decoder continue rather than commit early to EOT,
targeting the uniform under-emission residual directly.

capability_investigated:
The <|startofprev|> prompt slot (ledger iter_008/014/021) used with a
bidirectional payload — neighbour-window text from BOTH sides of the target
window — which requires a two-pass structure because in a single causal pass
the text after a window does not exist yet. Studied that the frozen surface
forwards an arbitrary [sot_prev, *ctx, sot, lang, task] prompt verbatim and
that scores[0] (return_scores) lets pass 1 classify each window's confidence.
what_i_learned:
All prior <|startofprev|> conditioning fed only causal text: the running
transcript (iter_008/021, which cascaded errors forward and regressed) or a
constant glossary (iter_014). A two-pass decode makes the full transcript
available, so a window's prev slot can carry its SUCCEEDING text too, and
because that pass-1 transcript is fixed the future-context bias cannot cascade
the way the running feed did. This is reachable entirely through the frozen
surface and is the conditioning lever for the substitution residual (no longer
a deletion problem: length_ratio 0.92-0.98).
hypothesis:
Swap iter_018's temperature-escalation fallback for a context fallback: pass 1
decodes every window once (temp-0 beam) into a full transcript, then each
gate-failing window (avg-logprob < -1.0 or compression_ratio > 2.4) is
re-decoded once with its neighbour windows' text in the <|startofprev|> slot,
keeping the higher-scoring decode. Bidirectional topical/vocabulary context
should reduce substitutions on the high-CER files (01_8088_10:01=0.28,
01_8098=0.26) while runtime stays bounded — pass 1 is one decode per window
(cheaper than the multi-temp escalation) and only bad windows pay one extra pass.

capability_investigated:
ct2 Whisper.generate's suppress_blank kwarg, forwarded untouched through the
frozen generate() **decoding_kwargs. It is distinct from iter_025's
suppress_tokens (a non-speech symbol ban): suppress_blank specifically bans
the leading blank/space token at the very first decode step. No prior iter
(001-026) ever set it; it sat at its ct2 default of True on every window.
what_i_learned:
suppress_blank=True (the default in force for all 26 prior iters) forbids the
decoder from emitting a blank as its first token, forcing an immediate
content-token commitment. That is harmless on the first window (which starts
in leading silence) but harmful on iter_007 re-anchored windows: they begin
exactly at a hard segment cut with no preceding audio (iter_015 cold onset),
so the forced first content token lands on a clipped utterance start and is
systematically mis-transcribed — a within-window substitution the boundary
fix cannot reach. The kwarg is reachable through the frozen surface and is
independent of beam_size, length_penalty, repetition_penalty, and prompt.
hypothesis:
Set suppress_blank=False on the decode so the model may emit a leading blank
at window onset instead of committing to a content token over the clipped
cold-onset audio. This targets the substitution residual (length_ratio
0.92-0.98 on every file, worst on the cold-onset files 01_8088_10:01 and
01_8098) that beam/length/anchor tuning never moved.

capability_investigated:
Not a generate() kwarg — the cut-location freedom of the frozen pipeline.
Studied that the WhisperProcessor pads any sub-30s input to a full 30s
window (ledger iter_002), so the workspace may feed segments of natural
length rather than fixed 30s / timestamp-stride blocks, and that the raw
waveform's frame energy is available to choose where cuts fall.
what_i_learned:
Because the processor zero-pads short inputs, a decode window does not have
to be a clock-aligned 30s block: variable-length speech segments cut at
silence are decodable through the unchanged frozen surface. This is the one
lever no decode kwarg can reach — every prior cut was placed by the decoder's
segment count, landing window edges mid-speech (the iter_015 cold-onset cause
of the substitution residual). Energy-VAD boundaries fall in silence on both
sides, so onset clipping and mid-sentence boundary deletion are removed by
construction, not by another beam/penalty tweak.
hypothesis:
Segment the waveform at silences (numpy frame-energy threshold; bridge sub-
0.35s gaps so no mid-sentence split; cap >28s runs at their quietest interior
frame; pad 0.12s each side) and decode each segment with the proven iter_018
beam+fallback decode. Every window now starts and ends in silence, which
should cut the cold-onset substitutions on the high-cer files (01_8088_10:01
0.28, 01_8098 0.255) that timestamp re-anchoring left behind.

capability_investigated:
The <|startofprev|> prompt slot (ledger iter_008/014/021/026) composed from a
NEW source: the truncated trailing segment that iter_007 re-anchoring drops
(token_ids after the last timestamp marker), rather than the full running
transcript, a constant glossary, or bidirectional two-pass text. Studied that
the dropped tail is precisely the audio span the next re-anchored window
re-decodes, and that the frozen surface forwards [sot_prev, *tail, sot, lang,
task] verbatim with no extra decode pass.
what_i_learned:
The re-anchor stride creates a per-window prev payload for free: the tokens
between the final timestamp marker and EOT are the exact utterance the next
window starts on cold (iter_015 onset clipping), so feeding only that tail as
<|startofprev|> gives warm linguistic context with a SINGLE-window horizon —
it cannot accumulate the window-to-window error cascade that made iter_008's
full-transcript feed regress, because each carry is consumed and replaced by
the immediately following window, and is cleared on any full-window step.
hypothesis:
Carrying the dropped trailing-segment text forward as <|startofprev|> context
conditions the cold re-anchored onset, reducing the within-window substitution
residual (the dominant error now that length_ratio is 0.92-0.98) on the high-
CER files (01_8088_10:01, 01_8098) without adding decode passes or risking the
drift that prior running-transcript conditioning incurred.

capability_investigated:
The waveform-slicing freedom of the frozen pipeline (processor zero-pads any
sub-30s input, ledger iter_002/028) combined with window-relative timestamp
values (ledger iter_007): specifically choosing each window's START sample
independently of where the transcript was committed, so a window can re-hear
audio it has already transcribed purely to supply acoustic context.
what_i_learned:
Every prior fix for the cold-onset substitution residual (iter_015) was
linguistic — startofprev tail (029), suppress_blank (027), glossary (014) —
or a decode kwarg; none fed the boundary segment its preceding AUDIO. Because
the frozen surface lets the workspace pick any window start, a fixed left-overlap
(win_start = committed - 1.5s) makes the segment the previous window re-anchored
to decode warm instead of cold, and the re-heard span is removable with no text
matching: drop tokens before the first timestamp marker whose window-relative
time >= the overlap boundary. Forward reach is preserved, so window count and
runtime are essentially unchanged.
hypothesis:
Feeding 1.5s of acoustic left-context before each re-anchored window and
trimming the re-heard segments by timestamp removes the onset clipping that the
exact-boundary cut imposed, lowering the substitution CER on the length-healthy
hard files (01_8088_10:01=0.28, 01_8098=0.255) that prompt/param levers stalled on.

capability_investigated:
The selection rule applied to multiple hypotheses from generate(). Every
prior multi-hypothesis iter (013 longest beam, 018/019 best sample, 023
longer beam) chose by max(scores[0]) avg-logprob or by length. Studied
using num_hypotheses on the sampling path (iter_019) to get N diverse
hypotheses in one decode, then selecting among them by inter-hypothesis
character agreement (difflib SequenceMatcher) rather than by the backend
score.
what_i_learned:
scores[0] (length-normalized avg-logprob) ranks hypotheses by decoder
confidence, not by correctness: a fluently-hallucinated substitution scores
ABOVE the correct-but-hesitant reading, so max-score selection systematically
keeps the over-confident outlier on exactly the low-confidence windows the
gate flags. Agreement across independent samples is an orthogonal, score-free
selection signal computable entirely in-process (stdlib difflib) from the
same hypotheses generate() already returns — no extra decode pass and no new
backend kwarg.
hypothesis:
Replace the temperature-escalation/best-score fallback with consensus
selection: on a gate-failing window draw _CONSENSUS_N=5 diverse samples in
one num_hypotheses pass plus the temp-0 beam result, and return the medoid
(max mean SequenceMatcher ratio to the others). The recurring reading across
draws should displace the single-hypothesis substitution that avg-logprob
rewarded, lowering CER on the substitution-dominated high-CER files
(length_ratio already healthy 0.92-0.98).

capability_investigated:
The ctranslate2.models.Whisper object returned by load() — specifically its
align(features, start_sequence, text_tokens, num_frames) method, which
force-aligns a given token sequence to the encoder audio frames and returns,
per WhisperAlignmentResult, a text_token_probs list. No prior iter called it;
only detect_language() (iter_022) ever used a non-generate() method, and every
hypothesis-selection iter (018/019/023/031) ranked by signals derived purely
from the decoder's own output (scores[0] avg-logprob, beam length, difflib
inter-hypothesis agreement).
what_i_learned:
align() exposes a per-token ACOUSTIC confidence (text_token_probs) computed by
matching each emitted token to the audio frames, which is a different axis than
the decoder's scores[0]. iter_031 established scores[0] is miscalibrated for
correctness — a fluent substitution scores above a correct hesitant reading —
so it systematically mis-selects on exactly the low-confidence windows the
fallback gate flags (the cer 0.21-0.28 substitution residual on the multi-window
files). align() probs are reachable through the frozen load() object with no
generate() kwarg, and as a teacher-forced single forward they are far cheaper
than a beam decode, so applying them only on gate-failing windows keeps runtime
near the current fallback cost.
hypothesis:
On clean windows keep returning the top temp-0 beam (no align() cost). On
windows that trip the avg-logprob/compression gate, force-align all five beams
(and any escalated temperature samples) and keep the hypothesis with the highest
mean text_token_prob instead of the highest decoder score. Audio-grounded
selection should pick the reading that actually matches the speech over the
over-confident substitution the beam committed to, lowering cer on the
substitution-dominated focus/high-cer files without trimming length.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s num_hypotheses sampling path (iter_019) feeding a difflib
token-level alignment (iter_031), but used to SYNTHESIZE a transcript rather
than to SELECT one hypothesis. Studied that the N sampled sequences_ids share
no required ordering, so they can be aligned to a common backbone and voted
position-by-position in-process — no extra decode pass, no new backend kwarg.
what_i_learned:
Every prior multi-hypothesis iter (019 best-score, 023 longest-beam, 031
medoid, 032 acoustic align) returns ONE whole hypothesis and therefore
inherits that hypothesis's own substitution tokens — selection cannot fix an
error that the kept hypothesis itself made. The N samples generate() already
returns support a strictly stronger operation: a per-token majority vote
(ROVER) over the difflib-aligned set produces a sequence no single member
equals, so a wrong token present in only the backbone is outvoted by the
diverse samples. This is reachable entirely through the frozen surface.
hypothesis:
On windows the avg-logprob / compression gate flags (the cer 0.21-0.28
substitution residual on multi-window files), draw _VOTE_SAMPLES diverse
samples in one num_hypotheses call, pick the medoid as alignment backbone,
and replace each backbone token with the majority vote across aligned
hypotheses (ties keep backbone). This corrects isolated substitutions that
whole-hypothesis selection structurally cannot, without altering clean-window
decoding or window count.

capability_investigated:
The waveform-slicing freedom of the frozen pipeline (processor zero-pads any
sub-30s input, ledger iter_002/028) used for OVERLAPPING fixed windows, then
difflib.SequenceMatcher (stdlib) over the surviving text-token ids
(id < endoftext, the timestamp/special-stripped sequences_ids) to stitch
consecutive windows on their shared span — a text-token merge, distinct from
iter_030's timestamp-time dedup and iter_031/033's same-window consensus.
what_i_learned:
Because each region is decoded twice — warm in one window's tail (up to 30s of
preceding context) and cold in the next window's onset — the seam overlap lets
the warm reading be kept and the cold-onset reading discarded by construction,
not by another decode kwarg. The matched overlap block partitions the two
windows: keep left through the match, take right only after it. This is the
one structure that lets the warm-tail version of every boundary win, which
re-anchoring (which always begins the next window cold at the cut) cannot do.
hypothesis:
Replace the timestamp re-anchor stride with 30s windows at a 25s stride and
stitch on the longest common text-token block. The cold-onset substitution
residual (iter_015, the unmoved length_ratio<1 0.92-0.98 cause) is eliminated
because no region's transcript is taken from a window that heard it cold.

capability_investigated:
The segment-end timestamp values in results[0].sequences_ids[0] (ledger
iter_007) reinterpreted as a per-window COVERAGE signal — how far into the
30s window the decoder kept emitting before EOT — rather than only as the
re-anchor advance point. Combined with the num_hypotheses sampling path
(iter_019) returning diverse hypotheses each carrying their own last
timestamp.
what_i_learned:
The last timestamp token's audio time is a direct, decode-free measure of
how much of a window the beam actually transcribed; on a full (non-final)
window a value far below the window edge marks early-truncation deletion,
which is invisible to the avg-logprob/compression gate (those flag
substitution and repetition, not a confidently-short transcript). Coverage
is therefore a deletion-specific fallback trigger AND a deletion-specific
selection axis — orthogonal to every prior selector (score, length,
agreement, acoustic prob), all of which can still pick a confidently-short
hypothesis.
hypothesis:
Add a coverage gate (last segment-end < 0.8 * window_seconds on a full
window) as a third fallback trigger, and on fallback select the
non-degenerate hypothesis with the DEEPEST last timestamp (tie-break by
score) from the temp-0 beam plus temperature samples. This recovers the
truncated window tail that drives the universal length_ratio<1, targeting
the long high-CER files (01_8088_10:01, 01_8098) where coverage is lowest,
while extra passes stay confined to truncation-suspect windows.

capability_investigated:
The Whisper object's align(features, start_seq, [text_tokens], num_frames)
text_token_probs (ledger iter_032) used as an acceptance gate over the full
num_hypotheses=beam_size beam list (ledger iter_013/023) from one decode pass,
rather than as a whole-hypothesis selector.
what_i_learned:
iter_023 (longest beam) and iter_032 (align mean prob) each regressed for
complementary reasons that cancel when combined: the longest beam is the most
likely to have hallucinated tokens, which is precisely the low-acoustic-prob
signal align() exposes; conversely align()-by-mean alone has no length
pressure so it keeps the short reading that causes the universal
length_ratio<1. The longest beam is therefore safely usable iff its align()
mean prob stays within a margin of the top beam's. align() runs at most twice
per window (only when the longest beam differs) and is a single
teacher-forced forward, cheaper than the beam pass, so runtime is bounded.
hypothesis:
Replace top-beam-only selection with acoustic-gated length recovery: from the
beam pass keep the longest hypothesis when its align() mean prob >= top - 0.08,
else keep the top. This directly attacks the residual universal length_ratio<1
(0.92-0.98 every file) without re-importing iter_023's over-generation,
leaving the temp-fallback gate unchanged downstream.

capability_investigated:
The load()-object's align(features, start_seq, [text_tokens], num_frames)
text_token_probs (per-token ACOUSTIC confidence, ledger iter_032/036)
combined with generate()'s return_no_speech_prob (encoder non-speech
estimate, ledger iter_010) used as the trigger that decides whether to align.
what_i_learned:
align()'s text_token_probs and the encoder's no_speech_prob are composable as
a localized TRIM, not just a whole-hypothesis selector/gate: on a window whose
no_speech_prob exceeds the silence gate, a trailing contiguous run of text
tokens whose acoustic prob collapses below a floor is text emitted over
silence, removable token-by-token. Prior align iters (032 selector, 036 beam
gate) returned whole hypotheses and fought deletion; trimming only the
low-acoustic tail on silence-suspect windows leaves real-speech windows and
their length untouched, and align runs once per suspect window so runtime
stays bounded to those windows.
hypothesis:
Gate align() on no_speech_prob > 0.5 and, on those windows only, drop the
trailing run of kept text tokens whose align() acoustic prob < 0.2. This
targets the harness-directed hallucination_hit focus files (text confabulated
past the real audio) without disturbing the universal length_ratio<1 residual
on speech-dominant windows.

capability_investigated:
The raw waveform amplitude fed into WhisperProcessor before any decode. The
HF Whisper mel front-end applies only a fixed affine to the log-mel
((log_spec+4)/4) and performs no loudness/peak normalization of the input
signal, so absolute waveform amplitude propagates untouched into the encoder
features. This input axis sits entirely before frozen.asr_backend and is
outside every generate() kwarg, prompt slot, and load()-object method the
ledger (iter_001-037) has exhausted.
what_i_learned:
Because the feature extractor does not loudness-normalize, varied-level phone
calls reach the encoder under-driven: a quiet call yields lower mel energy
and a constant-shifted log-mel, which the encoder cannot recover. Amplitude
is therefore a per-call conditioning variable no prior iter controlled — the
whole ledger held the waveform fixed and only changed decode behavior. This
is a candidate cause of the universal length_ratio<1 / substitution residual
that is worst on the hardest files (01_8088_10:01 lr=0.924, 01_8098 lr=0.927).
hypothesis:
Peak-normalize the full waveform once before chunking (scale so max|x|=0.95),
presenting every call a comparable full-range signal to the encoder. Sub-unity
target only lifts quiet/under-driven audio and never clips, so it should
improve features on the low-level hard files without distorting already-hot
ones — addressing substitution uniformly rather than via another decode tweak.

capability_investigated:
The decoder text-prefix slot of ct2 Whisper.generate — forced text tokens
placed AFTER [sot, lang, task] in the start sequence (openai-whisper's
`prefix`), as opposed to the <|startofprev|> soft-prompt slot BEFORE <|sot|>
that the whole ledger (iter_008/014/021/026/029) exhausted. Studied that the
backend forwards an arbitrary prompt id list verbatim and returns
sequences_ids that EXCLUDE the start sequence.
what_i_learned:
Because ct2 keeps the entire start-sequence (sot,lang,task + any appended
text ids) out of the returned sequences_ids, forced-prefix continuation
needs no de-dup: the carried tokens cannot reappear in the window's emitted
text, and the existing timestamp re-anchor logic operates unchanged on the
newly generated remainder. This makes the prefix slot a distinct, free
conditioning lever from <|startofprev|>.
hypothesis:
The residual length_ratio<1 (worst on lowest-LR files) is cold-onset
clipping at every re-anchor cut. Forcing the previous window's trailing kept
words as a decoder prefix makes the cold onset decode as a grammatical
continuation rather than from zero, recovering the clipped onset tokens.
Carry is short (4 tokens), gated on a confident window, and cleared on any
full-window/degenerate step so it cannot cascade like iter_008's feed.

capability_investigated:
The <|notimestamps|> decode mode of the frozen surface — a prompt composed as
[sot, lang, task, <|notimestamps|>] rather than the [sot, lang, task] the
whole ledger has used since iter_006. Every prior low-confidence fallback
(iter_018 temperature, iter_019 sampling) stayed inside the timestamped decode
mode; the timestamp-free mode itself was never decoded or compared.
what_i_learned:
Composing the prompt id list alone selects the decode mode: with
<|notimestamps|> appended, generate() returns sequences carrying pure text and
no <|t|> markers, so the decoder allocates none of its output budget to
segmentation and is not forced to commit EOT at a segment boundary. On a
low-confidence window this lets it keep transcribing the full 30s, recovering
trailing content the timestamped beam truncates early — the mechanism behind
the universal length_ratio<1 deletion residual. The two modes' outputs are
comparable in-process by char length and compression ratio with no extra pass.
hypothesis:
Replace iter_018's temperature-escalation fallback with a cross-mode one: on a
gate-failing window (avg-logprob < -1.0 or compression_ratio > 2.4 from the
single timestamped beam pass) re-decode the same features in notimestamps mode
and keep that text when it is longer and non-degenerate, stepping the full
window. Targets the length_ratio<1 deletion residual directly; the extra
decode is confined to gate-failing windows so runtime matches iter_018.
